verdict.summary: OAuth is only for Brex developer partners: there's no self-serve app console, so you apply to the partner program, sign an access agreement, and ask Brex developer support to issue a client ID/secret, register your redirect URIs and assign your scopes. A Brex customer can mint a user token for their own company in minutes, but that isn't a path for connecting other companies' accounts.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Even staging OAuth needs Brex-issued partner credentials. Brex publishes no timeline for partner acceptance or credential issuance. A user token on your own Brex account works in minutes for prototyping.

timeToProd.assumes: An agent reading card/cash transactions and expenses for other Brex customers through partner OAuth; customers automating only their own Brex account can use a user token the same day.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Partner program acceptance, the access agreement, credential and scope issuance by developer support, and Brex reviewing your demo video.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: There's no documented formal review beyond sharing a demo video. The total is our estimate because no Brex timeline is published.

prerequisites.item: Acceptance as a Brex developer partner
prerequisites.why: Partner authentication is only for Brex developer partners. Client IDs and secrets are issued by Brex developer support, not a self-serve console.
The launch checklist has partners sign the access agreement, which arrives by email, before development.

prerequisites.item: Exact redirect URIs and the list of APIs you need
prerequisites.why: Redirect URIs are supplied to Brex when credentials are set up and have to match exactly. Brex assigns the scopes for your client.

prerequisites.item: A demo video of the finished integration
prerequisites.why: The partner checklist asks you to share a demo video with Brex once the integration is built.

scopeTiers.impact: openid is required for OIDC requests and offline_access for a refresh token. Every scope needs partner credentials first.

scopeTiers.time: Assigned by Brex at credential issuance
scopeTiers.impact: What a spend-analysis or bookkeeping agent needs. Brex customers can grant none, some or all requested scopes at consent.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Scope strings come from scopes_supported in the live OIDC discovery document. The mapping to APIs is inferred from names.

scopeTiers.time: Assigned by Brex; likely more scrutiny
scopeTiers.impact: Lets an agent issue cards, set budgets or move money. Brex's prohibited and restricted activities list and transfer limits (1,000 transfers and 100 international wires per 24h) apply.

steps.title: Prototype with a user token on your own Brex account (optional)
steps.detail: As an account or card admin, accept the developer API agreement, then create a scoped user token under Developer > Settings in the dashboard. It's shown once and expires after 90 days without use.

steps.title: Draft the partner application
steps.detail: Describe the agent's use case, the Brex APIs and scopes needed (read-only where possible), the data handling and security posture, and the redirect URIs for staging and production.

steps.title: Apply to the Brex partner program
steps.detail: Submit the 'Become a partner' form or use 'Talk with the partner team' for technology partners.

steps.title: Wait for partner acceptance
steps.detail: Brex's partner team evaluates the request. No criteria or timeline are published.

steps.title: Sign the access agreement and request credentials
steps.detail: Sign the emailed access agreement, then contact developer support with redirect URIs to get a client ID/secret and assigned scopes for staging and production.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Read endpoints from https://accounts-api.brex.com/oauth2/default/.well-known/openid-configuration. Send a random state of 9+ characters and verify it on return. Optionally use PKCE (S256). Open consent in a real browser, not a webview or iframe. Request openid offline_access plus API scopes.

steps.title: Handle rotation, partial grants and rate limits
steps.detail: Store the new refresh token on every refresh (90-day lifetime, rotates on each use). Handle insufficient-scope and permission errors from partial grants. Back off with jitter on 429 and prefer webhooks over polling.

steps.title: Test in staging
steps.detail: Authorize against the staging auth server (accounts-api.staging.brexapps.com) and the api-staging.brex.com API. Staging data can be purged at any time.

steps.title: Record and share the demo video
steps.detail: Record the end-to-end connect flow and agent features, and share it with Brex as the checklist asks.

steps.title: Brex sign-off and production launch
steps.detail: Brex reviews the demo and production credentials are used for customer connections. Only Brex users with the proper roles can grant consent.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The checklist doesn't describe a formal approval step after the demo.

blockers.symptom: No 'create app' or client ID option anywhere in the Brex dashboard
blockers.cause: Partner OAuth credentials are issued only by Brex developer support to accepted partners. The dashboard only offers user tokens for your own company.
blockers.fix: Apply to the partner program and request credentials from developer support.

blockers.symptom: Consent fails or the user can't approve your app
blockers.cause: Only Brex users with the proper roles can grant permission to partner apps.
blockers.fix: Ask the customer to have an account or card admin complete the connection.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Exact role names weren't readable (the roles and permissions page returned 404).

blockers.symptom: Calls fail with insufficient-scope or permission errors after a successful connect
blockers.cause: The customer granted only some of the requested scopes, or the scope wasn't assigned to your client by Brex.
blockers.fix: Check granted scopes after token exchange, degrade gracefully, and ask Brex support to add missing scopes to your client.

blockers.cause: The URI doesn't exactly match one registered with Brex at credential setup.
blockers.fix: Send Brex support the exact URIs, including the staging and production variants.

blockers.cause: More than 1,000 requests per 60 seconds per Client ID and Brex account, or daily transfer/card limits. Brex may also lower limits.
blockers.fix: Exponential backoff with jitter, per-client token bucket throttling, and webhooks instead of polling.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 3600s. Refresh tokens last 90 days and rotate on every refresh. A lapsed refresh token means the user has to reauthenticate, so refresh idle connections before 90 days.

Brex moved hosts. API servers are api.brex.com and api-staging.brex.com, and the auth servers are accounts-api.brex.com and accounts-api.staging.brexapps.com (the transition began 2026-01-01). Treat the OIDC discovery document as the source of truth.
Client Credentials grants are only for the Onboarding API (referrals). Every API that touches an existing customer's data uses the Authorization Code grant.
User tokens (own-company use) expire after 90 days without an API call and stop working if the creating user is deactivated, so they're a poor base for a long-running agent.
Use random idempotency keys on create-transfer and create-card calls so an agent's retries don't duplicate money movement.
The Brex auth server is Okta-based. Its discovery document advertises many grant types, but Brex's partner docs only describe authorization code (optional PKCE) and client credentials.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Seen in the live discovery document (okta.myAccount.* scopes, many grant types).
